author: Chris Holcomb
text:
My personal experience has been this with the Libre. Very inconsistent readings. Multiple times gave me low reading when I was actually high and vice versa. Inability to calibrate to my fingerstick. Lost connection a lot and my phone is never more than 3 ft away from me. Even with all the "tricks" of applying of how and where. I've had 3 sensors fail on me. Due to trusting the Libre my A1C actually rose 2 points. Also the cost went up.
I got put back on the G7 15 day, I found out it was cheaper for me to pay out of pocket for my dexcom then to have insurance billed. I pay $175/month out of pocket compared to $298/month if insurance is billed. The libre went up to $275/month billing insurance and $600 if I paid out of pocket.

I understand that each person is different. I don't tell you my experience with libre to put fear or deter you from using it. I really do recommend making sure you do at least 2 finger sticks a day to see what the average point difference is.
